overview: Black declines with 2...Bc5 and develops, usually answering 3.Nf3 d6 with ...Nf6 and ...Nc6. White can play Nc3, Bc4 and d3 or c3 and d4, with an open f-file and an e5 pawn that may be hit by fxe5. Play is more open than a standard Italian but less forcing than the accepted lines.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nf3, Nc3, Bc4, then fxe5 or d4 to open the centre; the f-file adds pressure.
Pressure f7 along the a2-g8 diagonal.

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...d6, ...Nf6, ...Nc6, ...Bg4 and hit the f4 pawn or e4.
Counter in the centre with ...d5 when allowed.

typical_structures.structure: Open e-file after fxe5, or e4/f4 pawns against ...e5/...d6.

character.notes: Declined lines are quieter than the accepted ones but still open, with king safety on both sides in play.

gambit.notes: Black has not taken f4, so nothing has changed hands.

soundness.notes: Sound; Black equalises with sensible development.

structure.notes: Tension between e4/f4 and e5 with open lines likely; flexible.

approach.notes: A respectable if rarer way to meet 2.f4; strong players choose it to avoid chaos.

sublines_that_differ.name: Svenonius
sublines_that_differ.how: Pinning with a Bg4 pin; slightly sharper.

character.reason: Open development without the forcing tactics of the accepted lines.

gambit.reason: Declined, so no material has changed hands.

structure.reason: e4/f4 against e5 is tense and undecided.

approach.reason: A respectable declined line, less common but not offbeat.

level.reason: Plans are clear and theory is modest.
